column1: # House romanization "house/2" for planet/language/romanize.py (builder A 2026-11-03; re-drawn for book readers 2026-11-03).
# Deterministic. House rule: ASCII first, then digraphs, then diacritics; a letter that reads as something else in common
# orthographies (ę ǫ look nasal, ł reads w) is not used. Base sounds only: modifiers are composed in romanize.py (aspiration h,
# ejective ', labialized w, palatalized y (Hepburn ky, ny), prenasal m/n/ng before, voiceless sonorant h before, long consonant =
# first letter doubled (Hungarian ssz), long vowel = last letter doubled, tone: Yoruba-style acute high / grave low / mid
# unmarked, caron rising, circumflex falling, double acute extra-high, double grave extra-low).
# Nasal vowels: always a tilde (ã). A following n was considered and rejected: one rule for every lect, and it never reads as a
# coda n, whatever the lect's syllables.
# Book mode (romanize book=True; names.py `roman`): the book drops tone, writes a nasal vowel as vowel + n (plain before a
# nasal), doubles one long vowel per word, writes ə e, ɛ ɔ ɪ ʊ ɑ plain, ü ö only beside i e, and keeps one diacritic letter
# per word (uvular ġ x̣ always kept); lossy on purpose, the workbench and `roman_full` keep this table's full spelling.
# alt = the spelling used when the lect writes aspiration (it contrasts aspirated and plain): th, dh, kh, gh, sh, zh, ch, qh
# would then read as aspirates, so the fricatives take their single-letter forms. Velar and uvular never share a spelling
# (uvulars: q, qh, gq, nq, rq, and ġ for ʁ).
# contrast / marked: a sound written plainly (ɛ e, ɔ o, ɑ ɒ a, ɪ i, ʊ u, ɫ l, β v, ɦ h, ə e) takes the marked spelling only
# when the lect has the sound it would otherwise be confused with (romanize.contrasts_of names the contrast). marked_alt: the
# marked spelling when aspiration is also written (bh would read as breathy b). marked_tonal: the marked spelling in a tonal
# lect, where a grave would read as low tone (Yoruba ẹ ọ, Igbo ị ụ, tone marks go above). ə is ë beside e (Albanian), a when
# the lect has e but no a, e otherwise. Where ll or hh spells ɫ or ɦ, a long l or h is written with a middle dot (Catalan l·l).
# Non-human percepts are spelled in ASCII letters only, so a reader can say them (the IPA column keeps the exact symbol); the
# base letters lose their diacritics (ġ g, ò o) and a trailing mark is added:
#   growl / harsh phonation  rh   (a‼ arh, ɣ‼ ghrh, ʁ‼ grh: a snarl)      purr        rr   (aᵣ arr, mᵣ mrr)
#   second voice (syrinx)    wh   (aᴖ awh, ɹᴖ rwh: a warble)               sub-bass    mh   (a˯ amh, ŋ˯ ngmh: a hum)
#   ultra register           ih   (i˰ iih, s˰ sih: a squeak)
#   percussives: lip smack pk, teeth clack tk, beak knock ck.
# Where such a spelling could be read as a sequence of the lect's other sounds, the usual hyphen separates them (a-rr).
# convention = the real orthography or transliteration followed ("house" = coined here; "merge" = a documented merger).
